title: Equal-command three-ordinate family: broad-primary null and narrower-window tradeoffs
question: How does a fixed equal-command schedule family trade all-time and post-glass thermal floors in the released margin-shell phantom?
method: Prespecified nine schedules; nominal/high uniform Fe; both SAR readings; independent exact-horizon RK2 baseline then 36 discovery, 20 spatial and 10 time-refinement runs; separate myocardium/specimen endpoints and conditional sampled nondominance.
result: At 0.02 C/min tolerance, middle deficit is the sole sampled wider-primary nondominated discovery member in each scenario, conditional on terminal eligibility (no eligible nominal/clamped discovery schedule). Narrower supports retain four-member discovery frontiers and refined control/vertex tradeoffs. Storage-temperature minima can reward early duty while obscuring later performance. No robust or mechanical protocol is claimed.
limitations: Synthetic geometry and voxelization-sensitive terminal decisions
Uniform assumed Fe and adiabatic exterior
Only nine schedules and selected finer-grid subset; no continuum optimum
Both low-temperature SAR extensions remain uncertain
Wider rate floor is only over observed trajectories; 0 C crossings incomplete
No ice, stress, fracture, recovery or mechanical optimization evidence

scientific_assessment.limit: No demonstrated stress or preservation improvement.
